NONE: › to praise
讚美，讚揚，讚頌

example: The German leadership lauded the Russian initiative.
德國領導人讚揚了俄羅斯的倡議。

NONE: › (of actions and behaviour) deserving praise, even if there is little or no success
（行為）值得讚揚的，值得稱讚的

example: a laudable goal/ambition
值得讚揚的目標／雄心
The recycling programme is laudable, but does it save much money?
這項回收計劃值得稱道，不過它能節省許多資金嗎?

NONE: › expressing praise
稱讚的，讚揚的，讚美的
A2 to smile while making sounds with your voice that show you think something is funny or you are happy
（出聲地）笑，大笑
B1 the act or sound of laughing
笑；笑聲
› informal an enjoyable or funny activity
令人愉快的活動，好玩的活動
› mainly UK informal someone who is funny
好玩的人，有趣的人

example: They laughed at her jokes.
聽了她講的笑話他們都笑了。
I couldn't stop laughing.
我情不自禁地笑個不停。
I said he'd have to give a talk and he laughed nervously.
我告訴他說他必須發言，他聽後緊張地笑了起來。
She's so funny - she really makes me laugh.
她太有意思了——真讓我笑死了。
It's very rare that a book is so good you actually laugh out loud.
一本能讓你笑出聲來的好書真是不多見。
It was so funny, I burst out laughing (= laughed suddenly and loudly).
太有意思了，我放聲笑了出來。
I laughed till I cried.
我笑得直流眼淚。
a loud/nervous laugh
放聲大笑／緊張的笑
I was embarrassed at the time, but I had a good laugh about it later.
那時我很尷尬，但過後卻覺得非常可笑。
"How was the party?" "Oh, it was a laugh."
「派對辦得怎麽樣？」「哦，相當好玩。」
You'd like Sharon - she's a good laugh.
你會喜歡莎倫的——她這個人很風趣。

NONE: B1 to show that you think someone or something is stupid
取笑（某人），笑話（某人）
B1 to treat someone or something as if he, she, or it is not important or does not deserve serious attention
嘲笑（某人），蔑視（某人）

example: I can't go into work looking like this - everyone will laugh at me.
我不能這個樣子去上班——大家會取笑我的。
If you say that, people will just laugh at you.
如果你那樣說，人們就會看不起你。

NONE: › to make it obvious to someone that you do not respect them
當（某人）的面嘲笑

example: They'd laugh in your face if you suggested me for the post.
如果你提議讓我擔任這個職位，他們準會當面嘲笑你。

NONE: › to laugh a lot, very loudly
狂笑，爆笑
› to make yourself laugh about something unpleasant in order to make it seem less important or serious
對…一笑置之

example: She tried to laugh off their remarks, but I could see she was hurt.
她試圖對他們的話一笑置之，但我看得出她的內心還是受到了傷害。

NONE: › to secretly find something funny
竊笑，暗自感到好笑

example: They're very polite in your presence, but you get the feeling they're laughing up their sleeves.
當著你的面他們都很有禮貌，但你能感覺到他們在暗自發笑。

NONE: › to laugh a lot, loudly
大笑不止，狂笑不已

example: You laughed your head off when I fell!
我摔跤了，你卻笑個沒完！

NONE: C2 to laugh, shout, scream, etc. very noisily and for a long time
持續地大笑／喊叫／尖叫（等等）

example: There I was lying face down on the pavement and you two were laughing your heads off!
我就在那裡臉朝下趴在人行道上，而你們兩個卻在那裡大笑不止！

NONE: › silly and not deserving to be seriously considered
可笑的，荒唐的

example: Privately they thought the idea laughable.
私下裡他們覺得這個主意很荒唐。

NONE: nitrous oxide : a type of gas that is used as an anaesthetic (= a substance that stops pain)
› someone or something that seems stupid or silly, especially by trying to be serious or important and not succeeding
笑柄，笑料

example: Another performance like that and this team will be the laughing stock of the league.
如果下一場比賽表現還是那樣，這支球隊就會成為聯賽的笑柄。

NONE: › If you do something laughingly, you are laughing while you are doing it.
笑著，面帶笑容地
› disapproving If you say something is laughingly described in a particular way, you think this thing is so bad that it does not deserve the description.
冠冕堂皇地，裝模作樣地，荒唐可笑地

example: He laughingly pointed out our mistakes.
他面帶笑容地指出了我們的錯誤。
It is only one of the absurd rules in the system of law laughingly known as British justice.
這只是被冠冕堂皇地稱作英國司法的法律體系中荒唐的法律規定之一。

NONE: › the act or sound of laughing
笑；笑聲

example: She roared with laughter (= laughed very loudly).
她放聲大笑起來。
As we approached the hall we could hear the sound of laughter.
我們快走到大廳時可以聽到裡面傳出的笑聲。

NONE: › said to mean that trying to be happy is a good way to stop worrying
歡笑是良藥。

C: C1 an event to celebrate or introduce something new
啓動儀式，發布會，發表會
C1 an occasion when a ship is put into water, or a spacecraft is sent into space, for the first time
下水（船首次出航）；發射（火箭首次升空）
› a boat that has an engine and carries passengers for short distances, especially on a lake or a river, or from the land to a larger boat
（尤指河或湖上的）汽艇，遊艇，摩托艇

I or T: B2 [ I or T ] to begin something such as a plan or introduce something new such as a product

T: C1 [ T ] to send something out, such as a new ship into the water or a spacecraft into space

NONE: › to jump with great force
猛跳，猛地一躍，猛撲

example: How much champagne will we need for the launch?
這次發表會我們需要多少香檳？
Illness prevented her attending the launch party for her latest novel.
她因病無法出席爲她新近推出的小說舉辦的慶祝派對。
The launch of the space shuttle was delayed for 24 hours because of bad weather.
因天氣情況不佳，太空船的發射延遲了24個小時。
The programme was launched a year ago.
這項計劃是一年前開始實施的。
The airline will launch its new transatlantic service next month.
這家航空公司下個月將開闢一條新的跨越大西洋的航線。
A devastating attack was launched on the rebel stronghold.
向叛軍堡壘發起了猛烈的進攻。
[ + adv/prep ] UK After working for the company for several years she decided to launch out on her own and set up in business.
在為該公司工作數年後，她決定在商界自立門戶。
A spokesman for the dockyard said they hoped to launch the first submarine within two years.
船廠發言人說他們希望在兩年內讓第一艘潛艇下水。
to launch a missile
發射飛彈
The defender launched himself at the attacking player, bringing him to the ground.
防守隊員猛地撲向進攻者，把他摔倒在地。

NONE: › to start saying something or criticizing something with a lot of energy or anger
發起，開始（評說、批評等）

example: He launched into a verbal attack on her handling of the finances.
他對她的財務管理方式進行了一番抨擊。

NONE: › a special area from which spacecraft or missiles are sent into the sky
（火箭）發射台，發射架

example: The rocket blew up on the launch pad.
火箭在發射臺上爆炸了。
figurative Soap operas have long been a launch pad for film actors.
長期以來，連續劇一直都是電影演員走紅的跳板。

NONE: › a device that sends something such as a rocket or a missile into the air with force
發射器（用動力將火箭或導彈發射至空中的裝置）

example: a mobile rocket launcher
移動式火箭發射器

T: › to wash, dry, and iron clothes, sheets, etc.
› to move money that has been obtained illegally through banks and other businesses to make it seem to have been obtained legally

example: freshly laundered sheets
新洗的床單

官員們被指控在海外洗錢後將贓款轉回美國。

NONE: › a place where you pay to use machines that wash and dry clothes
洗衣店

待洗（或正在洗滌、洗完）的衣物

C: › [ C ] a business that washes clothes, sheets, etc. for customers

example: I've got to do (= wash) my laundry.
我要把衣服洗了。

NONE: › a large container in which dirty clothes are kept until they are washed
（裝待洗衣物的）洗衣筐，衣物筐
› a detergent in the form of a powder or liquid that is used for washing clothes and other things made of cloth
洗衣粉，洗衣液
› a person who has been given a very high honour because of their ability in a subject of study
（在某研究領域）獲得桂冠的人，獲得殊榮的人

example: a Nobel laureate
諾貝爾獎得獎者

C or U: › a small evergreen tree (= one that never loses its leaves) that has shiny leaves and small, black fruit
› praise for a person because of something they have done, usually in sport, the arts, or politics
（尤指在體育、藝術或政治方面獲得的）桂冠，榮譽，讚譽

example: The actors are very good, but when all is considered the laurels must surely go to the director of the play.
演員的表演很出色，但如果綜合考慮，這份榮譽應該授予該劇的導演。

NONE: › a circle of leaves that, in the past, was worn on the head by an important person or the winner of a competition
